claims.explanation: Amisulpride is a dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist, and its selective antiproliferative effect across cancer lines is most plausibly explained by DRD2 expression: lines with high DRD2 (and related dopamine-pathway) expression are sensitized, while low expression is protective. The transcriptional virtual cell similarity to dopamine receptor antagonists (eticlopride) supports an on-target DRD2 mechanism rather than a general cytotoxic effect. Mutation features such as TP53, PTEN, or BRAF are common across both sensitive and resistant lines and are therefore weak, non-specific predictors.

features.basis: amisulpride is a high-affinity DRD2 antagonist; target expression required for response
amisulpride binds DRD3 with high affinity (Ki ~3 nM)
dopamine/D2 signaling regulates prolactin; PRL pathway may bypass D2 blockade
TP53 mutation is frequent in sensitive lines but also in resistant lines, weak evidence
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines but also resistant lines, weak evidence
BRAF mutation in several sensitive melanoma lines but also in resistant lines, weak evidence
EGFR mutation in several sensitive lung lines but not specific
KRAS mutation appears in resistant pancreatic/colorectal lines but also sensitive lines, weak evidence
CTNNB1 mutation in several least-affected lines, weak evidence
NF1 mutation in several resistant lines but also sensitive lines, weak evidence
ARID1A mutation in several resistant lines but also sensitive lines, weak evidence
KMT2D mutation in several resistant lines but also sensitive lines, weak evidence
